message.content:
Roger presented for his initial intake session reporting that he is not feeling the greatest and is experiencing a difficult time focusing. He stated that when his focus feels off, many other aspects of his life feel off as well. The lack of focus was identified by Roger as particularly distressing to him.

We utilized psychoeducation regarding the interplay between cognitive impairment from traumatic brain injury and mood disorders to address his concerns. This intervention helped contextualize his symptoms within the framework of his disability. Roger responded by acknowledging the connection between his TBI and current struggles with concentration.

Roger disclosed that he is currently staying at the Turning Point shelter while collecting disability benefits for his traumatic brain injury. We discussed his history of substance use during the session. He reported no current desire to use substances because they cause too many problems in his life. His anxiety and depression scores were recorded at 2 and 3, respectively, which are considered mild ranges.
